title: Track Insurance Verification Requests (IVRs)

claims.claim: The vendor_coordinator or practice_admin role is required to create and update IVRs.
claims.finding: No practice_admin role exists. IVR Tracking is gated by the Inventory feature only (user-routes.tsx:2164-2168); status changes go through update_ivr_order_status_v2 with no role list in the page.
claims.proposed_text: Anyone whose role has the Inventory feature can update IVRs in IVR Tracking.

claims.claim: The product must exist in the Product Catalog with a valid HCPCS code; the Product dropdown lists only Active products with a HCPCS code, and the HCPCS populates automatically.
claims.finding: The IVR request product list filters by facility, category, vendor, status 0 and is_deleted — not by is_active or HCPCS (IVRInventoryRequestModal.tsx:467-476).
claims.proposed_text: Pick a product from the selected vendor's catalog for the chosen category; its HCPCS shows when the catalog has one.

claims.claim: IVR statuses move Submitted → Pending → Approved, or → Declined → Agreed.
claims.finding: The statuses are Pending, Incomplete, Agreed, Approved, Declined (IVRStatusUpdateModal.tsx statusOptions; update_ivr_order_status_v2 allows pending|incomplete|agreed|approved|declined). There is no Submitted status, and the page omits Incomplete. A new request starts as Pending (no outcome).
claims.proposed_text: IVR statuses: Pending (new), Incomplete, Approved, Declined, and Agreed.

claims.claim: Agreed means the patient and provider agreed to proceed at the patient's financial responsibility after a Declined decision, or the payer issued a formal agreement letter.
claims.finding: The code stores Agreed as an outcome with no stated meaning (IVRStatusUpdateModal.tsx; update_ivr_order_status_v2). The definition cannot be checked from code.

claims.claim: Open IVR Tracking from the Inventory Management hub.

Create an IVR with New IVR in the upper-right of the IVR Tracking table: select the patient (search by last name or DOB), select the product, enter the planned date of service, attach documents with Attach Documents, and click Submit IVR.
claims.finding: IVR Tracking has no create button (only Refresh, Filters, View, Update Status, Upload Response). IVR requests are created from the Wound Cockpit (WoundCockpitPage.tsx:51 lazy-loads IVRInventoryRequestModal) for the wound's patient: pick Product Category (Amniotic or Biologics), vendor, product, wound area, ICD-10, Clinical Justification, notes, then "Submit IVR Request". No date-of-service or Attach Documents step.
claims.proposed_text: Create an IVR from the patient's wound in the Wound Cockpit: pick the category, vendor and product, enter the wound area, diagnosis and clinical justification, and click Submit IVR Request. Track it in IVR Tracking.

claims.claim: When the payer acknowledges, set the status to Pending and enter the payer's reference number; when approved, set Approved and enter the authorization number.
claims.finding: The status modal has the five status buttons, Outcome Notes, and a vendor-response file upload; no reference-number or authorization-number field (IVRStatusUpdateModal.tsx:300-470).
claims.proposed_text: Open Update Status, pick the new status, add Outcome Notes (e.g. reference or authorization numbers), and optionally upload the vendor response.

proposed_checks.pattern: Update outcome and upload vendor response

claims.claim: If declined, set Declined and document the denial reason in the Notes field.
Setting Approved clears the product for use at the scheduled visit.
claims.finding: Approval auto-creates an inventory order and a pending receiving row (update_ivr_order_status_v2, migration 20261021120000 'On approval, auto-create the inventory order AND a pending receiving'). No code gates Visit Wizard use on an Approved IVR, so 'cleared for application' cannot be confirmed.
claims.proposed_text: Setting Approved creates an inventory order and a pending receiving for the product.

proposed_checks.pattern: -- On approval, auto-create the inventory order AND a pending receiving.

claims.claim: With an Approved or Agreed IVR, the product is highlighted at step 13 (Procedure Supplies) of the Visit Wizard.
claims.finding: Procedures & Supplies is section 11 (section_11_procedures_supplies, VisitWizardV4.tsx:845-848); section 13 is Medication Management. No IVR-based highlight in ProcedureSuppliesVisit.tsx was found.
claims.proposed_text: Remove, or: Approved IVR stock allocated to the patient is offered in the Visit Wizard's Conservative Care & Interventions picker.

claims.claim: The IVR Tracking table supports filtering by status, payer, and date range.
claims.finding: Filters are status, submission method (Fax, Email, Manual) and date range (IVRTrackingDashboard.tsx:443-485); no payer filter.
claims.proposed_text: The IVR Tracking table can be filtered by status, submission method, and date range, and searched by patient, wound, vendor, order ID, request ID, or product.

proposed_checks.pattern: placeholder="Search by patient, wound, vendor, order ID, request ID, or product..."

claims.claim: An IVR is a prior-authorization record tracking whether a payer approved a graft product for a patient encounter.
claims.finding: The product describes IVR Tracking as "Inventory Vendor Requests" — "Monitor and manage inventory vendor requests for wound care products" (IVRTrackingDashboard.tsx:377-379; hub tile text). Outcomes come from the vendor response; no payer field exists on the tracking screens.
claims.proposed_text: An IVR is a request to the product vendor to verify coverage for a graft for a patient; IVR Tracking records the vendor's outcome and response.

proposed_checks.pattern: Monitor and manage inventory vendor requests for wound care products

claims.claim: Status cannot be advanced from Declined to Approved until the payer issues a reversal.
claims.finding: Transitions are enforced by is_ivr_status_transition_allowed_v2 (raises IVR_STATUS_TRANSITION_INVALID), whose definition was not found in v1.1.345 migrations; cannot confirm which transitions are allowed.
